assessments.support: ABIDE is named as the autism dataset but no cohort N, sites, release (ABIDE I vs II), or exclusion/QC rule for the ABIDE subsample is reported in the available text (only ADNI's N=349 and Table 1 breakdown are given).

A detailed DTI/PANDA preprocessing pipeline and AAL-90 atlas are described for ADNI, and PANDA is also used as the comparison baseline for ABIDE (Table 6), but no equivalent preprocessing/atlas statement for the ABIDE data itself is given, and it is unclear whether ABIDE connectivity was derived from resting-state fMRI or structural data.

C-PAC pipeline, group-ICA-derived BFNs and dual regression are described in detail.

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort, pipeline and demographic/clinical reporting are thorough for this single-site (NYU) ABIDE-I subsample, but group-ICA/dual-regression feature derivation appears to precede the cross-validation split with no stated leakage control, and the single reported accuracy lacks an uncertainty interval; the deliberate single-site design avoids cross-site heterogeneity but means no site-generalization evidence is provided.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (ASD vs HC); ABIDE (consistent with ABIDE I), 871 of 1112 subjects (403 ASD, 468 HC)
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI parcellated with the Harvard-Oxford atlas; Fisher z-transformed Pearson connectivity, dimensionality-reduced via recursive feature elimination; a transductive population graph (nodes = imaging features, edges weighted by gender/age/acquisition site) classified with a proposed attention/skip-connection GCN (AN-GCN), evaluated with stratified 10-fold cross-validation against several GCN-based baselines.
narrative_row.outcomes: AN-GCN achieved 96.91% accuracy and 96.86% AUC on ABIDE, far exceeding the strongest compared baseline (DS-MML, 87.62% accuracy, 92.00% AUC) and the basic GCN baseline (64.63% accuracy).
narrative_row.key_limitations: No diagnosis-source statement; feature elimination appears to precede the CV split; site/age/gender used directly as population-graph edge weights rather than controlled for, with no leave-site-out evaluation; the very high accuracy is substantially above the paper's own baselines and typical ABIDE benchmarks, suggesting possible leakage/inflation.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Illustrates a predictive, transductive population-graph GCN approach on ABIDE with a pipeline/atlas clearly reported but validation design raising leakage concerns given an unusually high accuracy.
